detail.longDescription: I've been trying for some months to make something using some pretrained Gemma models, but I keep jumping from error to error, and I haven't even started the actual programming (haven't even gotten to play around with the models). My current issue is that when I try to run the example code from Kaggle , I get the following error: My Code: (which is really just the example code from Kaggle) import os import keras import keras_hub import tensorflow as tf # import kagglehub < this comment here was a band-aid fix for a previous error. os.environ["KERAS_BACKEND"] = "torch" # Or "tensorflow" or "jax". os.environ["XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_MEM_FRACTION"] = "1.00" model = keras_hub.models.Gemma4CausalLM.from_preset( "gemma4_instruct_2b", dtype="bfloat16", ) The Error (it's on jupyter, so the error is on line 1 of its cell): AttributeError Traceback (most recent call last) Cell In[3], line 1 ----> 1 model = keras_hub.models.Gemma4CausalLM.from_preset( 2 "gemma4_instruct_2b", 3 dtype="bfloat16", 4 ) AttributeError: module 'keras_hub.api.models' has no attribute 'Gemma4CausalLM' For this specific snippet and result, I'm on Python 3.14.4 -- keras_hub 0.19.0 -- keras 3.15.1 I also attempted the same snippet on Python3.10.0 -- keras_hub 0.25.6 with the same result I also tried other solutions I found online, such as switching Gemma4CausalLM to GemmaCausalLM and replacing "gemma4_instruct_2b" to "kaggle://keras/gemma4/keras/gemma4_instruct_2b" When I do this, the output is as follows: Downloading to /home/fern/.cache/kagglehub/models/keras/gemma4/keras/gemma4_instruct_2b/2/config.json... 100%|██████████| 4.50k/4.50k [00:00<00:00, 1.61MB/s] ValueError Traceback (most recent call last) Cell In[6], line 1 ----> 1 model = keras_hub.models.GemmaCausalLM.from_preset( 2 "kaggle://keras/gemma4/keras/gemma4_instruct_2b", 3 dtype="bfloat16", 4 ) File ~/projects/fernbot2.0/.venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/keras_hub/src/models/task.py:186, in Task.from_preset(cls, preset, load_weights, **kwargs) 179 raise ValueError( 180 "Do not call `Task.from_preset()` directly. Instead call a " 181 "particular task class, e.g. " 182 "`keras_hub.models.TextClassifier.from_preset()`." 183 ) 185 loader = get_preset_loader(preset) --> 186 backbone_cls = loader.check_backbone_class() 187 # Detect the correct subclass if we need to. 188 if ( 189 issubclass(backbone_cls, Backbone) 190 and cls.backbone_cls != backbone_cls 191 ): File ~/projects/fernbot2.0/.venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/keras_hub/src/utils/preset_utils.py:642, in KerasPresetLoader.check_backbone_class(self) 641 def check_backbone_class(self): --> 642 return check_config_class(self.config) ... 489 "classes with `register_keras_serializable()`." 490 ) 491 return cls ValueError: Attempting to load class keras_hub>Gemma4Backbone with `from_preset()`, but there is no class registered with Keras for keras_hub>Gemma4Backbone. Make sure to register any custom classes with `register_keras_serializable()` I'm guessing there's an issue with my Keras_hub version, and that's why it doesn't recognize Gemma4? But when I try to force upgrade to something like keras_hub 0.28.0 using pip install keras_hub==0.28.0 keras==3.13.0 , the terminal says "ERROR: Could not find a version that satisfies the requirement tensorflow-text; platform_system != "Windows" (from keras-hub) (from versions: none) ERROR: No matching distribution found for tensorflow-text; platform_system != "Windows" for context, I am on WSL Ubuntu using virtual environments. I have both versions of python installed on WSL (3.10 and 3.14) and I just use different commands to make the virtual environments ( python3.10 -m venv .venv for python 3.10 and python3 -m venv .venv for python 3.14) so perhaps there is an issue with my tensorflow install?
